conventions: The ASV supplies a conditional *if* inside the וְהִנֵּה protasis of the examination formula — *and, behold,* ***if*** *the plague be spread* — where the Hebrew writes no conjunction at all. That *if* is its own `added` unit in all sixteen places (13.3, 5, 6, 8, 10, 13, 17, 20, 25, 30, 32, 34, 36, 39, 43, 55) and is never folded into the waw that opens the clause, into הִנֵּה, or into the verb. Where the clause does write אִם (13.21, 22, 23, 26, 27, 28, 35, 37, 53, 56, 57), כִּי (13.16, 31, 40, 42, 51) or a waw (13.49, 58), that morpheme takes the *if* and nothing is added. The italicized *yet* of 13.40 and 13.41 and the surplus *whether* of 13.55 are the same case.

רָאָה + אֵת and רָאָה + verbal suffix are aligned differently in this chapter, and the source licenses the difference. Where the object marker stands, it takes the *on* or *upon* by which *look* reaches its object under rule 16 (13.3, 6, 15, 25, 30, 31, 32, 34, 43, 50, 51, and the *unto* of 13.49). Where the object is instead a pronominal suffix on the verb itself and no marker is present, the particle stays inside the verb's unit and the suffix takes only the pronoun (13.5, 17, 21, 26, 27, 36). Every other אֵת in the chapter is `unrepresented`, the ASV writing its object bare.

The metonymic הַנֶּגַע, 'the plagued person', is rendered *him that hath the plague* (once *that which*, 13.50). Where an article morpheme stands on the noun, the article takes *him that* / *that which* and heads on the pronoun under rule 41, while the noun keeps *hath the plague* (13.4, 12, 13, 17, 33, 50). At 13.31 the same metonym is the anarthrous construct of נֶגַע הַנָּתֶק — the phrase's only article stands on הַנָּתֶק — so no article is present to take that English and the whole supplied *him that hath the* joins the substantive's own unit under rule 46, headed on *plague*. Read which word the article morpheme sits on before treating the two as a split.

The intensifying infinitive absolute takes the adverb the ASV writes for it and is not folded into the finite verb: פָּשֹׂה תִפְשֶׂה → *spread*(finite) + *abroad*(infinitive absolute) at 13.7, 22, 27 and 35, פָּרוֹחַ תִּפְרַח the same at 13.12, and טַמֵּא יְטַמְּאֶנּוּ → *surely* at 13.44. *Abroad* is read as the infinitive absolute's own rendering rather than as a phrasal particle of *spread* under rule 44, because the ASV writes it only where the infinitive absolute stands: פָּשָׂה alone is *be spread* throughout (13.5, 6, 8, 20, 23, 28, 32, 34, 36, 53, 55).

מִחְיָה is the ASV's *quick* and חַי its *raw* throughout the chapter: בָּשָׂר חַי → *raw flesh* (13.14, 13.15 twice, 13.16), מִחְיַת הַמִּכְוָה → *the quick flesh** with *flesh* italicized (13.24), and מִחְיַת בָּשָׂר חַי → *quick*(מִחְיָה) *raw*(חַי) *flesh*(בָּשָׂר) at 13.10, corrected by this reconciliation pass from an earlier reading that had the two reversed.

promotions.summary: Settles the subordinating conjunction the ASV supplies for a clause whose Hebrew writes none — the conditional *if* of a וְהִנֵּה protasis, and the italicized *yet* of a bare asyndetic clause — as its own `added` unit, and forbids folding it into the waw, into הִנֵּה, or into the verb to avoid the `added`. Rules 42 and 51 already dispose of a surplus *and* and a supplied *also* this way; nothing in the contract covered the subordinator, which is the ASV's commonest supply in casuistic law.
promotions.basis: LEV.13 supplies the word eighteen times with no morpheme in the clause to license it: sixteen *if*s in the וְהִנֵּה protasis (13.3, 5, 6, 8, 10, 13, 17, 20, 25, 30, 32, 34, 36, 39, 43, 55) and the italicized *yet* of 13.40 and 13.41. Against that stand seventeen clauses in the same chapter where אִם, כִּי or a waw is present and takes the ASV's *if*, *when* or *that*, so the rule's condition is exercised in both directions inside one chapter. The corpus agrees and does not contradict: וְ is aligned to *if* three times (1KI.8.33, 8.35 and one more) and to *when* five times, and כִּי and אִם take their subordinators as ordinary aligned units, so the rule never strands a present morpheme. The two clauses at 13.40 and 13.41 carry an ASV italic on *yet*, which corroborates under rule 7 without being relied on.
promotions.rule: **A subordinating conjunction the ASV supplies for a clause whose Hebrew writes none is `added`.** Casuistic law opens its protasis with אִם, with כִּי, or with a waw, and where one of these stands in the clause it takes the ASV's *if*, *when* or *that* by rules 14 and 30: the corpus aligns a waw to *if* and to *when*, and כִּי takes whichever of them the ASV has written for it. But the ASV also writes such a word for a clause that has no conjunction in it at all — *and, behold,* ***if*** *the plague be spread* for וְהִנֵּה פָּשָׂה הַנֶּגַע, and the italic ***yet*** of *he is bald,* ***yet*** *is he clean* for קֵרֵחַ הוּא טָהוֹר הוּא — and there no morpheme licenses it: it is its own `added` unit under rule 30. Do not fold it into the waw that opens the clause, into הִנֵּה, or into the verb, for the reason rule 42 gives about a surplus *and* and rule 51 about a supplied *also* — the word is written beside those renderings rather than inside one of them, and the waw and הִנֵּה already have the *and* and the *behold* the ASV wrote for them. Count the clause's conjunctions against the ASV's subordinators, as rule 42 counts waws against *and*s, and mark whichever side is in surplus. An ASV italic on such a word corroborates it, and the absence of one is not evidence against it, by rule 7.

report: One real cross-verse split, at LEV.13.10. The chapter renders חַי by *raw* wherever the two words stand together — בָּשָׂר חַי → *raw flesh* at 13.14, 13.15 (twice) and 13.16 — and renders מִחְיָה by *quick*, as 13.24 shows, where מִחְיַת הַמִּכְוָה → *the quick flesh** has *flesh* italicized as an ASV supply. LEV.13.10 alone reversed both: for מִחְיַת בָּשָׂר חַי → *there be quick raw flesh* it gave *raw* to מִחְיָה and *quick* to חַי. Nothing in the source licenses the reversal, so 13.10 is patched to *quick*(מִחְיָה) / *raw*(חַי) / *flesh*(בָּשָׂר), which also leaves the unit contiguous. The verse's own review note had weighed a different competing reading (giving *quick raw* wholly to מִחְיָה) and never tested the lexeme assignment against 13.24.

Groups checked and found licensed rather than split. רָאָה + אֵת gives the marker the *on*/*upon* (13.3, 6, 15, 25, 30, 31, 32, 34, 43, 50, 51) while רָאָה + verbal suffix keeps the particle in the verb's unit (13.5, 17, 21, 26, 27, 36); the difference is which morpheme is present. The metonymic הַנֶּגַע takes *him that* on the article under rule 41 at 13.4, 12, 13, 17, 33, 50, and at 13.31 the same metonym is the anarthrous construct of נֶגַע הַנָּתֶק, so the supplied *him that hath the* joins the substantive under rule 46 — morphology, not a split. בַּ before *the seventh day* is unrepresented where the ASV writes a bare adverbial accusative (13.5, 6, 27) and *in*/*on* where it writes one (13.32, 34, 51). קָרַחַת heads on *bald* and גַּבַּחַת on *forehead* consistently at 13.42 and 13.43; 13.55's *within*/*without* is the ASV's own recasting, flagged in its margin. כָל כְּלִי fuses to *anything* five times and splits at 13.58 only because the ASV writes *whatsoever thing*, which is rule 30's one-English-word condition working as written.

The 23 added units — which the lemma table cannot see — are internally consistent. Sixteen are the conditional *if* supplied inside a וְהִנֵּה protasis that writes no conjunction; in every clause that does write אִם, כִּי or a waw, that morpheme takes the *if* and nothing is added. Three are a surplus *and* before לֹא פָשָׂה where no waw stands (13.5, 23, 28); the parallel clauses that do have a waw (13.6, 32, 34, 55) align it. The rest are the appositional *even* of 13.38 (no object marker present to license it), the italicized *yet* of 13.40 and 13.41 (no waw), and the surplus *whether* of 13.55, whose single אוֹ has already taken the written *or*, exactly as the chapter's אוֹ pairs take *either* and *or* one word apiece.

No BSB disagreement is a genuine error. The R, Rd, Td and Sp3ms recurrences are the documented convention difference — BSB attaches the preposition, article or suffix to its phrase where the ASV writes no English for it — and each was checked against the ASV line: 13.7 and 13.13 write no connective for their waw, 13.15 writes *the raw flesh is unclean* with the subject noun explicit and no second pronoun, 13.33's אֵת stands on a bare object, and 13.38 writes *the skin of the flesh* rather than *their flesh*, which is why its Sp3mp is unrepresented while 13.39's takes *their*. No accepted edge was changed to improve the rate.

Five conventions recorded, all of them judgments a verse aligned from the log alone would not have had; the validation report showed 0 recorded against 40 repeating notes. One promotion returned: the supplied subordinator, which this chapter produced eighteen times and which rules 42 and 51 already dispose of for a surplus *and* and a supplied *also* without covering.
